塔潘鼓是一種源自中東和巴爾幹地區的傳統打擊樂器，在土耳其、阿拉伯世界及南斯拉夫地: The tapan is a traditional percussion instrument from the Middle East and the Balkans, widely found in Turkey, the Arab world and the former Yugoslavia. This large drum is usually made with a wooden body and animal hide, and has a low, penetrating tone.
塔潘鼓為雙面膜鳴鼓，初學先以繩索將鼓側掛於身上，使左右手各能觸及一面鼓皮。演奏通: The tapan is a double-headed membranophone; a beginner first hangs the drum at the side of the body with a rope, so that each hand can reach one head. Playing usually uses two sticks: the dominant hand holds a thick stick and strikes the thicker head for a deep, solid accent; the other hand holds a thin stick and strikes the thinner head for light taps and fine rhythms. The first points for a beginner are holding the drum steadily, dividing the work between the two hands, and practising the contrast in timbre between thick and thin sticks. In Balkan practice the non-dominant hand can phrase melodic statements while the dominant hand stresses particular beats.
塔潘鼓的歷史可追溯至中世紀，最初在奧斯曼帝國時期被廣泛使用，特別是在軍事和宮廷音: The history of the tapan goes back to the Middle Ages; it was first widely used in the Ottoman period, playing an important part especially in military and court music. As the empire expanded, the instrument's use spread through the whole Mediterranean and the Balkans. The tapan has a place in folk music, dance and religious rites.
塔潘鼓的鼓殼以硬木製成，可能使用胡桃木或栗木，其他木材依地區而異；木材經煮水後彎: The shell of the tapan is made of hardwood, perhaps walnut or chestnut, with other woods used according to region; the wood is boiled and bent into a cylinder and fixed in shape. The heads are mostly goatskin stretched in a round wooden frame; one head uses goatskin for a high sound, the other may use sheepskin, calfskin or donkey hide for a low sound, and other accounts favour wolf or dog skin. A rope runs in a zigzag through the shell, joining the two heads and also serving to tune them; metal rings or a strap can help with tuning, and there are rings and a band of rope for hanging the drum. The beaters are a thick walnut stick and thin sticks of willow, dogwood and other soft woods.
塔潘鼓音色深沉而富有力度，具有溫暖的低頻特徵。其鼓聲厚實渾厚，帶有明顯的穿透力，: The tapan's tone is deep and forceful, with a warm low end. Its stroke is thick and full and carries well, and each strike sets up a lasting resonance. Beside light hand drums or bright small drums, the tapan sits lower and sounds steadier and heavier.
塔潘鼓（Hornbostel–Sachs 211.212.12）屬膜鳴雙面鼓，以: The tapan (Hornbostel–Sachs 211.212.12) is a double-headed membranophone struck with beaters, common in West Asian and Balkan music. In Macedonia it mostly accompanies the zurna and the gaida bagpipe; in Bulgaria the gaida and the gadulka fiddle, and it appears at weddings, patron-saint celebrations and as a solo in folk dances. The folk dances of Romania, Moldova and Hungary also use it. In Turkey, Armenia and Azerbaijan it often plays with the zurna, and it is part of Janissary military music. The Levantine dabke dance, the zaffe wedding entrance and the groom's alada entrance pair it with the mijwiz, the minjayra flute, the mizmar and the darbuka goblet drum; Assyrian folk dance music in Iraq is likewise mostly accompanied by the zurna.

The body is made of hardwood, the two heads are tensioned with rope, and a thick stick and a thin stick draw the low and the high sound respectively. Players often hang the drum across the side of the body on a rope strap and strike one head with each hand. The tapan is a large double-headed membranophone, H-S 211.212.12. The body is made of hardwood, the two heads are tensioned with rope, and a thick stick and a thin stick draw the low and the high sound respectively. Players often hang the drum across the side of the body on a rope strap and strike one head with each hand. It is common in West Asian and Balkan folk music, in Macedonia, Bulgaria, Albania, Romania, Moldavia, Hungary, Turkey, Armenia, Azerbaijan, the Levant and Iraq, where it accompanies weddings, festivals, dance and folk bands, and it can also play solo.
進入現代社會，塔潘鼓已成為世界音樂交流的橋樑，在當代世界音樂、融合音樂及民族音樂: In modern society the tapan has become a bridge between musical worlds, and it continues to play an important part in contemporary world music, fusion and folk music performance, standing for the meeting and continuation of Eastern and Western musical cultures.
鼓面的張力使其能夠產生層次豐富的音響效果，既能發出濃郁的低音基調，又可通過不同的: The tension of the heads gives the drum a rich layering of sound: it can lay down a strong bass foundation, and it can change colour with the striking position, moving from muffled and heavy to relatively bright. Its resonance rests on the air vibrating inside the shell, which gives the sound enough projection. In folk ensembles the tapan is often paired with other percussion, laying a deep, forceful rhythmic foundation for the whole band; its tone sits between a bass drum and a folk drum.
